title: The S3-compatible login takes the username from the credential string and then follows a path where the signature is never checked
index_line: T-0075 · AUTH_DECISION · AWS4-HMAC Authorization header: username parsed from Credential, signature check skipped → crushadmin · java · corroborated
invariant_violated: The S3 compatibility layer assumed that a header beginning AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 had already been through signature verification, so it used the Credential field only to name a user; the step that proves the caller holds the secret key was skippable for the header shapes the parser accepted.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated request carries `Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=crushadmin/` — no signature, no session cookie
the handler trims the header, tests only the AWS4-HMAC prefix, and splits the Credential field on '/' to obtain a user name
the extracted name must be a valid CrushFTP account without a '~'; the default administrator crushadmin qualifies
for this header shape the flow never reaches HMAC signature evaluation, so no key material or password is required
the request proceeds as the resolved user, so administrative endpoints answer without a password or session
as crushadmin the attacker creates backdoor accounts and uses the file manager, reaching code execution

source.http.header.value: the Authorization header: the S3 Credential field is the only place the user name comes from

sink.file.write.value: the administrative session the bypass grants writes server-side users/config and uploads files — the demonstrated impact surface behind the auth decision

guard.signature.value: the AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 signature check that the vulnerable flow never evaluates

oracle.channel.value: an authenticated admin API response (e.g. getUserList) returned without any cookie or password

preconditions.expr: the web interface answers over HTTP
the build contains the S3 authentication branch that keys on the AWS4-HMAC prefix
a bare Credential header is accepted as an authenticated admin request

success: an administrative API returns user/group XML with no cookie and no password
the response differs from the unauthenticated baseline in a way only an admin session produces
failure_like: the server rejects a user name that carries a '~' but the tester cannot name another account
false_positive: a 200 carrying the login page is not a bypass — require an authenticated payload (user list, admin XML)
a cached or CDN-served admin page is not evidence; compare against a fresh unauthenticated request

hazards: every product that speaks an S3-compatible API grows a second authentication path beside its native one
the tell is credential parsing by string split before any cryptographic verification
the alternate path usually resolves a principal, so the bypass escalates straight to whatever that principal can do
non_transfers: implementations that verify the signature before resolving the principal
deployments that disable the S3 compatibility listener

evidence.target: CrushFTP 10 before 10.8.4 / 11 before 11.3.1, S3-compatible authentication path (CVE-2025-31161 / formerly CVE-2025-2825)

provenance.author: ProjectDiscovery Research
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2025-31161 (published as CVE-2025-2825, renumbered; the post states all technical details still apply): the handler only checks that Authorization startsWith "AWS4-HMAC", splits the Credential field to obtain the username, and never evaluates the signature in the vulnerable flow

provenance.author: Huntress Labs
provenance.corroborates: same mechanism described operationally: any CrushFTP user name without a "~" in the Credential field, followed by "/", is accepted; the currentAuth cookie is not used by the bypass; crushadmin access yields backdoor accounts, file access and code execution

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2025-31161 description, CVSS and affected ranges
